recipes.name: Slow Cooker Lemon Garlic Chicken
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Mix together oregano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Rub spice mixture all over chicken breasts. Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook chicken until lightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes per side.
Place chicken in a slow cooker.
Mix water, lemon juice, garlic, and bouillon in the same skillet; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on Low for 6 hours or High for 3 hours. Add parsley to the slow cooker 15 to 30 minutes before the end of cook time.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Lemon Garlic Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This slow cooker lemon chicken is made with herb-rubbed chicken breasts simmered in a crock pot with lemon and garlic for an easy weeknight dinner.

video.description: Meet the perfect one-pot weeknight chicken dinner.

review.reviewBody: WOW this was good. I followed posters suggestions and used 2C water and dissolved a boulion cube in it. I also added a little white wine, the garlic and a shallot to deglaze the pan b4 adding the water/spice mixture. Even then, I had to add about a cup more water while it was cooking. I also dredged the chik breasts in a lemon pepper seasoning in addition to the oregono. I omitted all the salt from the recipe too, since boulion is so salty. Made the leftover broth into gravy, cooked up the Uncle Bens Chicken rice, and dinner was AbFab!! I will def be making this again!

This chicken is truly delicious. I have made this recipe four or five times already, it's definitely a keeper. It doesn't make much extra sauce so if you want some to scoop over potatoes or pasta you should double the sauce. The only thing I do differently is I use boneless skinless chicken tenders instead of chicken breast halves. The chicken pieces are smaller which allows them to soak up more of the juices and seasonings making them very flavorful and tender. I have also added sliced mushrooms... yum.

My first crock pot experience, and it turned out great! I took a lot of advice from the posts here: I covered the bottom of the pot with potatoes, onions, mushrooms, and lots of garlic (about 6 cloves). I used bone-in breasts (I did brown them first, using butter, salt and lemon-pepper mix, awesome), then deglazed the pan with 1 cup white wine. Added all that to the pot, along with 2 cans of chicken stock, 6 tablespoons lemon juice, and a little more salt. I cooked on high for 2 hours, then low for 1 hour - perfect! I think the bone-in chicken made a big difference, it was wonderful and falling apart. I would be careful with the lemon juice - I love strong flavors and was tempted to add more, but my 6 tablespoons was bordering on too bitter - excellent though! Also turned the extra juice into gravy for veggies and it was yummy, with side of chicken couscous!

What a dish! I doubled the spices except the garlic and used the juice of an entire lemon, and used chicken stock instead of water/boullion, using enough stock to almost cover chicken. And 30 min. before cook time finished, I stirred in 2 T. cornstarch dissolved in 1/4 cup water. Plenty of sauce for serving with chicken over pasta. And here's a trick: it was REALLY lemony and too sour, so I stirred in almost 2 T sugar. Totally fixed that problem. It was DIVINE!!! Thanks for an awesome, interesting recipe.

I've made this recipe (as written) a dozen times at least. I really liked it and it was a big hit with the fella. I began slowly adding ingredients to see what else I could do with this recipe, and I've reached a point where it's evolved into something unrecognizable from the original recipe. I started out following the ingredients and directions to a T and would serve over noodles (usually fettuccine but sometimes egg noodles). Then I started adding a little white wine to de-glaze the pan (per people's suggestions in the comments). After that came the addition of peas, carrots and mushrooms, which made my boyfriend love it even more, ESPECIALLY when I served it over egg noodles. One night, I asked my man what he wanted for dinner and he said he wanted the "sorta chicken stroganoff" I make all the time. It took me a minute to decipher that this was the recipe he was talking about. This comment from him was what inspired it's final form... I began adding sour cream and/or cream cheese to the sauce at the end of the cook time, as well as a bit of pickle juice, and the recipe is now a chicken stroganoff with more veggies. I love this recipe as it is written, and I love it even more now that it's evolved into "sorta chicken stroganoff" to my boyfriend and I. Thanks so much for this recipe Carla Joy!
I took suggestions from others and thickened the sauce. It tasted really similar to chicken piccata, so I added some capers to it before serving. Yum! And Easy!!

I did make a few changes like used chicken broth instead of water and the bouillion (2 cups). Cooked the breasts whole instead of half and more garlic and lemon juice and I broiled them after with parmeasean cheese and thickened the sauce. The most moist delicious chicken ever. Melted in our mouths. Whole family loved it.

You need 2 cups of liquid with this. I used 1 c. chicken broth, and 1 c. of white cooking wine. Three hours on high is good. The last 15 minutes I added shell pasta and broccoli cuts, and the parsley and a sprig of fresh rosemary. Yummy. Do not try to cook this without the extra liquid. Read the one star reviews. I love this recipe, and make it and save it, as I am a one person household now.

I took reviewers' suggestions: 2c water into pan to deglaze, made a gravy with 2tb each butter and flour. Added more water as needed. SO good. I'd double the sauce next time. Recipe is good AS WRITTEN too! I cut my chicken into large bite sized pieces.
The slow cooker is useless here. Do it as directed, but instead of transferring chicken and sauce to slow cooker, add chicken back to sauce and simmer till cooked through. Add parsley at the end.

I made this for company and it came out fantastic. The chicken was flavorful and not dry or rubbery, as some reviews are reporting. I DID use the additional instructions/ingrediants that were suggested in the video. Also, I thickened the broth it was cooking in with a little bit of cornstarch about half-way through the cooking process. I reduced the cooking time to 5 hours on low, and that was plenty. I waited until about halfway through the cooking time to add the carrots and peas (I skipped the mushrooms) to prevent that from becoming too soggy. I served over seasoned rice. Everyone loved it!
Great eating!

I made this recipe a few times already. I made it stove top, slow cooker and in the oven. All came out delicious. For busy families slow cooking is better but if you have at least an hour to spare after work before dinner my take is oven baked. Just prepare ahead of time . I put potatoes wedges on the pan with the chicken and served with a a nice cucumber salad or orzo Greek salad. Yummy

Nice flavor. Like others, I doubled the sauce and thickened it with a little cornstarch slurry. I am glad I didn't double the lemon and kept it at three tablespoons. I recommend being careful with the salt if you are like me and prefer things not to be very salty. I did cook this entirely on the stove but think it would be even better in the slow cooker so the chicken has time to really get tender.
No changes

This had great flavor and was easy to prepare. I did find the cook time a bit off for the size boneless skinless chicken breasts I was using. These were done at 1 hour at HIGH if I let mine go longer, the chicken would have been overcooked and dry. Be sure to adjust cook time according to the size boneless skinless chicken breasts you have. I had 4 breasts that weighed about 2 pounds all together. Next time, I would thicken the sauce with a little cornstarch at the end, as it was thinner than I would have liked. Otherwise, this is a tasty dinner!
Great flavor and easy to make.
I followed the directions and set crockpot to low. The chicken was lacking flavor and dry.

well I did not fallow the recipe exactly. I put a whole chicken in crockpot with salt and pepper with slices of lemon ( 2 lemon) then I looked up recipes and found this one so saw that up had more ingredients so I add what I had that was on your list I put it on for 8 hours on high in crockpot it smells good looking forward to eating it this afternoon
Quick preparation then came home from work to a delicious meal! Served with rice and there was even a little lemon sauce left over to spread on top!
